That phrase is the intent element of common-law burglary: unlawfully entering a building or dwelling "with the intent to commit a felony therein." Under the common-law definition, the felony doesn't have to be carried out. The intent has to exist at the moment of entry. Many modern statutes broaden it to any crime, including theft, so the exact wording depends on the jurisdiction.
